title: Lennox Furnace Code 200: Rollout circuit hard lockout
meaning: The rollout circuit is open, or had opened, and the furnace is in hard lockout.
commonCauses: A blocked flue or combustion-air path
A damaged or restricted heat exchanger
whenToCallPro: Leave the furnace off and call a licensed technician for a combustion-safety inspection.
dangerNote: Keep the furnace off. Do not reset a rollout switch. If you smell gas or a carbon-monoxide alarm sounds, leave the building and contact emergency services or the gas utility.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 200 means the rollout circuit is open, or had opened, and the furnace is in hard lockout on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Lennox integrated controls covered by installation instructions 508001-02D.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 201: Indoor blower communication failure
meaning: The furnace cannot communicate with the indoor blower motor.
commonCauses: Loss of power or communication to the blower motor
Damaged motor wiring or an incorrect control configuration
diySteps: Turn furnace power off and replace a visibly dirty filter.
Restore power once and listen for the indoor blower; do not reach into the blower compartment.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the blower does not run or the communication fault returns.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 201 means the furnace cannot communicate with the indoor blower motor on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Lennox integrated controls covered by installation instructions 508001-02D.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 220: Pressure Switch Open on Startup
meaning: The pressure switch did not close when the inducer started.
diySteps: Inspect vent and intake.
Check pressure switch tubing.
Clear condensate from trap.
whenToCallPro: Replace a failed pressure switch or inducer if obstructions are ruled out.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 220 means pressure switch did not close when the inducer started. Most often from blocked vent. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $175–$900.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 221: Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
meaning: The pressure switch remained closed when the inducer was off.
diySteps: Drain water from pressure tubing.
Inspect vent for restrictions.
Reset power once.
whenToCallPro: A stuck pressure switch should be replaced.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 221 means pressure switch remained closed when the inducer was off. Most often from stuck switch diaphragm. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $175–$550.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 270: No-flame retry lockout
meaning: The furnace exceeded its maximum ignition retries without sensing flame and entered soft lockout.
commonCauses: A dirty or weak flame sensor
diySteps: Confirm the thermostat is calling for heat and the gas shutoff has not been moved.
Turn furnace power off for five minutes, restore it once, and note whether the same code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed technician if ignition fails again after one reset or if you smell gas.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 270 means the furnace exceeded its maximum ignition retries without sensing flame and entered soft lockout on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Lennox integrated controls covered by installation instructions 508001-02D.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 271: Pressure-switch retry lockout
meaning: The furnace exceeded its ignition retries after the pressure switch opened.
commonCauses: A blocked intake or exhaust vent
A restricted condensate drain or pressure hose
A weak inducer motor or pressure switch
diySteps: With the furnace off, check outdoor intake and exhaust openings for snow, ice, leaves, or nests.
Replace a visibly dirty air filter, restore power once, and note whether the code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the vent is clear and the pressure-switch code returns; combustion-air testing requires instruments.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 271 means the furnace exceeded its ignition retries after the pressure switch opened on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Lennox integrated controls covered by installation instructions 508001-02D.

commonCauses: A blocked intake or exhaust vent

snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 272 means the furnace exceeded its recycle limit after a pressure switch opened on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 273: Flame-failure recycle lockout
meaning: The furnace exceeded its recycle limit after losing the flame signal.
commonCauses: A dirty or weak flame sensor
Unstable gas pressure or burner flame
diySteps: Confirm the gas shutoff has not been moved and the furnace panel is fully seated.
Try one reset and watch whether the burners light and then shut off again.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if flame drops out again or ignition becomes delayed or noisy.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 273 means the furnace exceeded its recycle limit after losing the flame signal on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Lennox integrated controls covered by installation instructions 508001-02D.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 274: Limit-circuit recycle lockout
meaning: The furnace exceeded its recycle limit after the limit circuit opened or stayed open too long.
commonCauses: A dirty or overly restrictive air filter
Closed or blocked supply and return vents
A blower, limit switch, or airflow problem
diySteps: Turn the furnace off and replace a dirty filter with the size and type specified for the system.
Open all supply registers and make sure return grilles are not blocked before trying one reset.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the limit code returns; repeated overheating can damage the furnace.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 274 means the furnace exceeded its recycle limit after the limit circuit opened or stayed open too long on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Lennox integrated controls covered by installation instructions 508001-02D.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 275: Out-of-sequence flame lockout
meaning: Flame had been sensed out of sequence; the flame signal is now gone and the furnace is in soft lockout.
commonCauses: A gas valve leaking or stuck open
whenToCallPro: Turn the furnace off and call a licensed technician immediately to test the gas valve and flame-proving circuit.
dangerNote: Turn the furnace off and do not reset it. If you smell gas, leave the building without operating switches and contact the gas utility or emergency services from outside.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 275 means flame had been sensed out of sequence; the flame signal is now gone and the furnace is in soft lockout on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Lennox integrated controls covered by installation instructions 508001-02D.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 277: Gas Valve Fault
meaning: The control detected an error in the gas valve circuit.
whenToCallPro: Gas valve faults require licensed repair.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 277 means control detected an error in the gas valve circuit. This is an emergency — do not attempt DIY repairs. Call a licensed technician immediately; typical repairs run $350–$900.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 278: Control Board Error
meaning: The integrated control reported an internal fault.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect for water near the board.
Ensure condensate is draining properly.
whenToCallPro: Board errors typically require control board replacement.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 278 means integrated control reported an internal fault. Most often from power surge damage. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $300–$800.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 279: Low Flame Signal
meaning: The flame current dropped below the minimum threshold.
diySteps: Clean the flame sensor.
Check return airflow.
Run one test cycle.
whenToCallPro: If flame current stays low, gas pressure and venting should be checked.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 279 means flame current dropped below the minimum threshold. Most often from dirty flame sensor. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $100–$400.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 280: Auxiliary Switch Open
meaning: An auxiliary limit or safety switch in series opened.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect auxiliary switches near the burner.
Do not bypass safety switches.
whenToCallPro: Auxiliary switch faults need a technician to identify which safety opened.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 280 means An auxiliary limit or safety switch in series opened. Most often from tripped rollout switch. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $150–$600.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 441: Blower Communication Fault
meaning: The board lost communication with an ECM blower motor module.
diySteps: Turn off power.
Reseat blower harness connectors.
Verify the blower door is secure.
whenToCallPro: ECM communication faults often require blower motor replacement.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 441 means board lost communication with an ECM blower motor module. Most often from failed ecm module. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $450–$1200.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 442: Inducer Speed Fault
meaning: The inducer did not reach the commanded speed.
diySteps: Inspect vent for blockages.
Listen for abnormal inducer noise.
Clear ice or debris at the vent cap.
whenToCallPro: Inducer speed faults may require motor replacement.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 442 means inducer did not reach the commanded speed. Most often from blocked vent. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $400–$900.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Lennox Furnace Code 443: Condensate Blockage
meaning: The condensate drainage system triggered a safety lockout.
diySteps: Clear the condensate trap.
Check the drain hose for kinks.
Empty or reset the condensate pump if present.
whenToCallPro: If drainage is clear but the code persists, the pressure switch or pump may have failed.
snippetAnswer: Lennox furnace code 443 means condensate drainage system triggered a safety lockout. Often caused by clogged condensate trap. Usually safe to try basic checks yourself; professional repairs run $150–$450.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.
